blocks.text: In 1677, two Brahmin ministers did the unthinkable. They convinced a muslim sultan to fund the revival of Hindu temples across the Carnatic. But their plan went deeper. They used the sultan's own Gold to systematically dismantle foreign control and empower native Hindu leaders. When Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj arrived in Hyderabad to seal this alliance, terrified the Mughal emperor Aurangzeb. He branded the brothers infidels and declared a brutal holy war to crush them. This is the forgotten story of Arcana and modern.

Akkanna & Madanna Akkarasu Banuji Pantullu and Madhava Banuji Pantullu, known to history Akkanna & Madanna, were born into absolute poverty. in Hanumakonda They were Niyogi Brahmins, a sub caste known for taking up secular, administrative and military roles. Above all, they were Mulkeies, the true sons of the soil while the Persian elite looked toward Iran. These brothers grew up in the dusty markets of the Deccan. Madina started his career as a bookkeeper, but he was a brilliant man of the pen.

He mastered the complex accounting and bookkeeping systems of the state. More importantly, he was a polyglot who mastered the Persian language better than the foreigners who ruled over him for 160 years. Golconda had been a Persian colony and spirit that QutubShahi rulers consider themselves junior partners to the Safavid Empire of Iran. The name of the Safavid Shah was even mentioned in the Friday sermons. Persians, Arabs and Turkomans held an absolute monopoly over the revenue. The treasury, the military, and the judiciary.

A regular shipping link existed between the Shah kingdom and Safavid Iran. Shahi vessels plied annually between Putnam and Blunderbuss on the Persian Gulf. Naturally, there was a continuous influx of traders, religious scholars, and mercenaries from Iran. They were accorded warm welcomes and often left the state much richer than when they arrived. The archetype of this era was Mir Jumla. The son of a poor oil seller from Iran, he used the Golconda machinery to become the richest man in the sultanate.

He owned the mining rights to every diamond in the kingdom, control the global diamond trade, and even licensed the export of native Hindus as slaves to European colonies. When he was finished plundering, he defected to the Mongols, taking the legendary Kohinoor with him. To men like me, Mir Jumla. The local population was just a resource to be harvested. Akkanna saw this divide clearly. In a rare candid moment with a Dutch merchant who had mastered the local Telugu tongue. He said, you can judge which government serves the country better, ours or that of the Muslims.

ours worked for the welfare of the land. Theirs is to grow rich and then leave for the lands they call thier Fatherland or Holy Land. For the 17th century, this was the very progressive sentiment. It sounded like a proto nationalism. Akkana was drawing a line in the sand between those who belong to the soil, and those who merely came to extract the resources. Madanna saw this rot from the inside while working as a secretary for the finance Minister, Syed Muzzafar. He eventually caught the eye of the Sultan Abdul Hasan,

who felt his own authority waning under the minister. In 1674. they struck in a bloodless political maneuver. Madanna helped the Sultan regain control of his own government. Madanna ousted his former boss in a coupe and was appointed Peshwa by the Sultan. Taking the royal name Soorya Prakasha Rao after nearly two centuries. A native Hindu had broken the glass ceiling. The Persian nobility was stunned. The sons of the soil were finally in control.

When Madanna took the reins, the economy was a nightmare. The primary source of revenue was land tax, but the state wasn't collecting it directly. Instead, they used the Izara system, a brutal form of tax farming. Agricultural lands, villages and even rich ports were auctioned off to the highest bidder for a lump sum paid to the state. These traders, mostly Persian nobles and wealthy merchants, had no interest in the long term health of the land. They paid the central government upfront and then used every form of extortion to extract a profit.

They often employed local native intermediaries for taxed farming at the district or village level. These traders also employed an army of Niyogi Brahmins as accountants and bookkeepers. The very class Madanna belonged to. As an insider, he was uniquely positioned to fix the rot. Madanna’s solution was revolutionary. He abolished the Izara system and replaced short term auctioneers with salaried government officials, local Hindus and Muslims

who actually cared if the villagers survived in some deserted villages. He offered a nine year, zero tax policy to entice the farmers to return from the forest and restart agriculture. He then turned to the diamond mines. Before him, 60,000 people worked in these mines, essentially as slaves. Madanna centralized the mines under the state and provided workers with thatched roof homes, dignity and real salaries. Despite Mughal claims, the Sultan wasn't a prisoner. Under Madanna guidance, the Sultan took frequent tours to connect

with his subjects in the most far flung areas of the kingdom. While rebuilding the heart of the Deccan, the brothers turned their gaze to the coast. For years, the Dutch, French and English had treated the Coromandel Coast like a playground, bribing their way out of taxes and disrespecting local authority. The French in particular, were problematic upstarts too good of Shahi authority. On June 27th, 1674, acting under Madanna’s

guidance and supported by Dutch naval power Qtubshahi, Commanders struck to recapture Saint-thome from French. This form stance alarmed the English in nearby Madras. The English governor Baron thought he could continue the old ways by evading taxes through bribes to check the English. Madanna plays his nephew linganna, now in charge of the strategic Poonamalay district Arcana. The master of the accounts personally audited the English East India Company's records. When the English continued their defiance Poona, patience snapped.

He ordered a total blockade of Madras and canceled their lease. Suddenly, the arrogant English were cut off. They realized that under this administration, bribery was dead. They immediately submitted, accepted Madanna’s terms, and paid their fines. Madanna repeated blockades against the British in 1678 and 1680. He treated native and foreign traders as equals, shattering the European notion of racial superiority. It is no wonder European traders hated the brothers and frequently

complained about Brahmin dominance in the QutubShahi ports. While the Persian nobility advocated for aggressive action against the Marathas, Madanna held a sacred vision that transcended quote, politics. He saw Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj not as a rival but as a protector of their civilization, while serving the Muslim QutubShah. Madanna convinced the Sultan to fund Shivaji s mission to restore Hindu power in the Carnatic

and establish a mutual defense against the Mughals. He sought to utilize Shivaji, its military genius, to achieve a higher purpose. The revival of the civilisational memory of the Nagara Empire in March 1677, when Shivaji Maharaj arrived in Hyderabad, the brothers personally received him at the city gates as a brother in arms. Madanna and Arcana conducted him into the city and subsidized his entire southern gambling deduction, Digvijay using the Sultan's treasury and artillery.

During this campaign, shivaray repaired and revived countless temples. Thanks to this alliance, many ancient temples of South India are preserved to this day. This action didn't sit well with the Emperor Aurangzeb, who fashioned himself “arch enemy of Brahmins” To protect this vision. Madanna Decentralize the power of jaggirdars, those who were known for switching sides. He built the professional Shahi on me, paid directly by the treasury, slowly reducing reliance on ill equipped and ill trained

Jagirdari armies. He also fixed a deep seated injustice for decades. A Mulki soldier was paid only one fourth of what a Persian adventurer had received. Madanna art immediately doubled the local salaries. He built a massive force and regularly trained them in the brutal boulder filled terrain around Hyderabad to ensure the army stayed loyal to the land. He appointed Akkanna as commander in chief, a move that further enraged the displaced Persian generals.

Akkanna and madanna the builders of the temples throughout the sultanate. There is the Grand Maha Kali Temple inside Hyderabad's walls and Akkanna build a massive Shiva temple at Maheshwaram, considered a masterpiece of its era. This spiritual revival was the heartbeat of the land, but to Aurangzeb, it was a declaration of war against his beliefs. He claimed the Sultan, being a Shia, had lost his way and failed to see the line between infidelity and Islam. These acts of devotion became Aurangzeb's ultimate pretext

for invasion. Madanna was an ultra patriot, but he sought alliances with local converts to Islam against the foreign mercenaries who had been draining the land for centuries. There is documented evidence of synods issued by Madanna for Muslim religious institutions, and Madanna even built an expensive Ashur khana for Shia muslims. In 1681, Prince Akbar, the emperor's own son, sought refuge with somebody.

This brought the full fury of Aurangzeb to the Deccan. He arrived with the vast army, expecting to crush his enemies in weeks. But some resistance against Mughals was legendary and he received secret monetary help from the Shah. Aurangzeb realized that as long as the Deccan stood together, he could never win. Mughal attention turned to the fractured Adil Shahi Sultanate at Bijapur, but Madanna was steps ahead. He guided Sultan Abu al-Hassan to propose a triple alliance.

Somebody would reinforce Bijapur while 40,000 Shahi horsemen would meet the Mughals in the field for the defense of Bijapur. The emperor's rage turned into an obsession when he intercepted a secret letter from Sultan Abdul Hassan to his agent and Ouija board. It confirmed that instead of being the Mughal tribute, Golconda was spending its wealth to save its neighbors. Meanwhile, the displaced Persian nobility, the men Madanna had ousted,

fled to Aurangzeb's court with a long list of grievances inventing stories of religious oppression, persecution. To beat the emperor, they were received by Aurangzeb sympathetically and assured of full justice. Consequently, Mughal chroniclers invented justifications against Akkanna and Madanna, painting them as infidels oppressing Muslims. The Mughals entered Hyderabad on October 8th, 1685, thoroughly looting the rich city unopposed.

Instead of defending his people, the Sultan fled to Golconda Fort. Corrupt officials and extremists sought their opening, blaming the Brahmin ministers for the city's ruin Akkanna and Madanna were murdered while returning to their home. Their houses were burned and a large scale Brahmin genocide took place both inside and outside the city. Their bodies were tied to the horses and dragged through the streets of Hyderabad. Madanna head was sent to Aurangzeb as a trophy. Aquino's head was placed under the foot of an elephant and crushed.

Many other Hindus, particularly Brahmins, lost their lives and property in the aftermath. Aurangzeb lived up to his label as the “arch enemy of Brahmins” The atrocities that followed were too graphic to describe here. Aurangzeb called them bigots, but they were never anti-Muslim. They encouraged Deccan Muslims. They were ultra patriots who believed the wealth of the Deccan belonged to the people of the Deccan. Within a year. Aurangzeb would personally invade the Golconda Sultanate again and absorb it into his empire.
